---
title: "Development and how to contribute"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r data}
repo <- "https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr"
projects <- utils::read.csv("data/projects.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tasks <- utils::read.csv("data/starter-tasks.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

organ_names <- c(
  kidney = "Kidney", liver = "Liver", pancreas = "Pancreas",
  "kidney-pancreas" = "Kidney-pancreas", heart = "Heart", lung = "Lung",
  "heart-lung" = "Heart-lung", all = "All organs", none = "Not organ-specific"
)

split_organs <- function(x) strsplit(x, ";", fixed = TRUE)

# The tables are hand-edited, so check them before drawing anything from them.
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(projects$issue),
  !anyDuplicated(tasks$issue),
  all(grepl("^[0-9]+$", c(projects$issue, tasks$issue))),
  all(unlist(split_organs(c(projects$organs, tasks$organs))) %in% names(organ_names)),
  all(tasks$role %in% c("verify", "supervise new")),
  all(nzchar(unlist(tasks[c("question", "deliverable", "needs", "done")])))
)

issue_link <- function(n) sprintf("[#%s](%s/issues/%s)", n, repo, n)
sentence_case <- function(x) paste0(toupper(substr(x, 1, 1)), substring(x, 2))

# Issue searches are built here rather than typed by hand, so every link uses
# the same encoding. Several values in one label: qualifier means "any of".
search_link <- function(text, ...) {
  query <- paste(c("is:issue", "is:open", ...), collapse = " ")
  sprintf("[%s](%s/issues?q=%s)", text, repo, utils::URLencode(query, reserved = TRUE))
}
label <- function(...) sprintf('label:%s', paste0('"', c(...), '"', collapse = ","))
```

sRtr is in early development (version `r as.character(utils::packageVersion("sRtr"))`, before
its first CRAN release), so functions and their arguments can still change.
Most of the code is written by Claude, an AI model, and reviewed by an
automated ChatGPT review and by the maintainer, Vagish Hemmige. What sRtr needs
most from people is judgment: checking that a calculation matches its source,
and deciding what a definition should be. Neither needs much R, and most of it
needs no SRTR data.

This page lists tasks you can start today, then every open project.

# Start with one of these

Each of these has a defined finish, and none needs SRTR data.

```{r starter, results = "asis"}
role_text <- c("verify" = "Verify existing work", "supervise new" = "Supervise something new")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(tasks))) {
  t <- tasks[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("## %s (%s)\n\n", t$title, issue_link(t$issue)))
  cat(sprintf("*%s; %s.*\n\n", role_text[[t$role]],
              paste(organ_names[split_organs(t$organs)[[1]]], collapse = ", ")))
  cat(sprintf("- **Question:** %s\n", t$question))
  cat(sprintf("- **What you produce:** %s\n", t$deliverable))
  cat(sprintf("- **What you need:** %s\n", t$needs))
  cat(sprintf("- **Done when:** %s\n\n", t$done))
}
```

# How to take one on

1. Comment on the issue with one sentence saying what you will do, for example
   "I can check the PDRI coefficients against the paper and post my
   comparison."
2. A maintainer replies with the scope, who will review it, and what to post.
   Please wait for that reply before starting substantial work.
3. Post your result on the issue. A comparison, a reading of the options or a
   short note is a complete contribution, even if it never becomes a code
   change.

Pull requests are reviewed by an automated ChatGPT review and merged by the
maintainer; a pull request cannot be merged until that review has run. If
you are a trainee working with the maintainer, start through your usual
supervision channel instead of a public comment.

# Keep SRTR data out of public places

Most tasks need no SRTR data. Tasks labelled `needs SAF access` need your own
access to SRTR's standard analysis files, under your own data use agreement
(DUA) with SRTR.

Never post patient-level data, or anything that looks like it, in an issue or a
pull request. Real results go on GitHub only as aggregate counts with no cell
from 1 to 10, and only when no hidden cell can be recovered by subtracting one
posted number from another. [Checking sRtr on your own
SAFs](checking-your-safs.html#share-counts-only) explains how to do this.
Made-up examples and zero counts are fine.

# Find work by organ

```{r organ-links, results = "asis"}
organ_rows <- setdiff(names(organ_names), c("all", "none"))
cat(paste0("- ", vapply(organ_rows, function(o) {
  search_link(organ_names[[o]], label(paste0("organ: ", o), "organ: all"))
}, character(1)), collapse = "\n"), "\n")
cat("- ", search_link("Not about any organ's data", label("organ: none")),
    ": geography, the website and the package's own setup\n\n", sep = "")
```

Each organ link includes the methods that apply to every organ, such as joins
and outcome definitions. To find something you can finish without SRTR data,
open `r search_link("tasks you can verify without SRTR data", label("role: verify"), label("no SAF needed"))`
or `r search_link("decisions and designs to supervise without SRTR data", label("role: supervise new"), label("no SAF needed"))`.

# All projects

Each project is a GitHub issue that lists its tasks and says who is working on
what.

```{r projects, results = "asis"}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(projects))) {
  p <- projects[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** (%s). *%s; %s.* %s\n", p$project, issue_link(p$issue),
              sentence_case(p$type),
              paste(organ_names[split_organs(p$organs)[[1]]], collapse = ", "),
              p$summary))
}
cat("\n")
```

# What the labels mean

Every task on GitHub carries four kinds of label.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `organ: ...` | The organ whose data the task concerns. `organ: all` means a method for every organ's data; `organ: none` means the task is not about any organ's data. |
| `role: verify` | Check existing or generated work against a known answer, such as a paper, a published table or a real-data run. |
| `role: supervise new` | Decide what should be built, or judge whether a new design or definition is right. Claude drafts the options. |
| `complexity: low`, `medium`, `high` | How complex the thing being checked or built is: one function with a known answer, several pieces or a judgment between options, or shared machinery many analyses depend on. |
| `no SAF needed`, `needs SAF access` | Whether finishing the task needs your own access to SRTR data. |

Project types (data handling, outcomes, geography and so on) are written on
each project issue and in the list above, not as labels.
